explanation: Append every new value to a dynamic array and sort the whole array after each insertion. Query the entries at floor((n-1)/2) and floor(n/2), averaging them; those indices coincide for odd size.
timeComplexity: O(n log(n+1)) general sorting upper bound per insertion of the nth value and O(1) per query. This code re-sorts the entire array instead of maintaining heaps.
spaceComplexity: O(n) stored values, with up to O(n) additional sorting workspace depending on the language/runtime.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: After each insertion, sorting restores the array as all inserted values in nondecreasing order, including duplicates. The chosen indices are exactly the two central positions for even n and the same central position for odd n. Their average is therefore the required median.
walkthrough: Insert 9 to get [9]. Insert 3 and sort to [3,9], whose two middle entries average to 6. Insert 12 and sort to [3,9,12]; both middle indices are 1, so the next query returns 9. Outputs are [6,9]. The arrays describe calls on one instance in order; expected contains only FindMedian results, and values entries for queries are ignored.
edgeCases: A median query requires at least one insertion.
Even counts require an average, which may be fractional.
Negative values and duplicate values remain ordinary stream entries.
